_comment: Master Mobile Plan (2026) > Recovery Measures > Point Release > Test Case IDs 'CC Reinstall Needed 6' ('Install 2.49.4, verify no forced update') and 'CC Reinstall Needed 7' ('Install 2.49.5, verify forced-update message'), as labeled under the 'Point Release' section of coverage_matrix.csv (a third, separate reuse of the literal 'CC Reinstall Needed N' ID text - see point_release_flow.yaml's header for the sheet-quirk explanation; row 8 of this same section already has a flow). THIS IS A DOCUMENTED GAP, NOT A RUNNABLE PRE-STEP, for the same structural reason as cc_reinstall_needed_provisioning.json and cc_update_needed_provisioning.json: both rows need a specific historical CommCare APK physically installed before any on-device Maestro assertion is possible - no HQ API call substitutes for that.
gap: Row 6 needs CommCare 2.49.4 installed and asserts NO forced-update prompt appears (i.e. 2.49.4 is presumably still >= whatever minimum CC version was configured at the time). Row 7 needs CommCare 2.49.5 installed and asserts the forced-update message DOES appear. Both require the exact historical APK staged on the device before the flow runs, same limitation as the CC Reinstall/Update Needed sections' row-1 gaps.
how_to_stage_it: python scripts/download_apk.py --tag commcare_2.49.4 --out apks/commcare_2.49.4.apk   # for row 6
python scripts/download_apk.py --tag commcare_2.49.5 --out apks/commcare_2.49.5.apk   # for row 7

then adb install -r <apk> onto the device manually/out-of-band, same caveat as the 2.45 provisioning files: this repo's run_suite.py/browserstack_client.py pipeline only stages one current-under-test APK per BrowserStack build, with no wiring to also pre-install a second, older APK into that same session.

tags_verified_via_gh_cli_2026_08_05.note: Both tags exist and were confirmed live via gh CLI (not guessed) - commcare_2.49.4 and commcare_2.49.5, exactly matching the sheet's row 6/7 version numbers with no ambiguity (unlike the '2.45' case, there's no patch-digit guesswork here since the sheet already specifies .4 and .5). Whether each tag's GitHub release actually ships a usable .apk asset (per download_apk.py's asset-naming-inconsistency caveat) was not individually re-checked - verify with --tag before relying on it in a real run.
